lens: visionOS / spatial glass: layered translucent panels, depth, the call as a floating window
name: Spatial Glass Call Window
one_liner: A dark, floating call window with a glass persona orb at its center and a coach HUD held in space around it, so practice feels like a spatial instrument instead of a chat app.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed visionOS: layered translucent panels, four depth tiers, and the call as a floating window. Research changed three things. First, Mobbin call peers split between dark canvases (PlayAI, Vapi) and light ones (ElevenLabs, Hume), so the dark live stage is our signature choice, not a category norm. Second, the debrief and dashboard default to light "paper-glass" for reading and printing. Third, text-heavy panes stay about 80 percent opaque so transcripts keep contrast. Council self-scores (1-10): A look 8, B UX 7, C unique 8, D live coaching 5.4 (conditional on the coach channel shipping), E library and wizard 5.5. Business: F1 SaaS 4.5 (crowded, price pressure), F2 entity sales 6.5 (white-label call window for training firms and call centers), F3 not worth building 3.5 (leans worth building).

design_language.typography: Sora 600-700 for display headings and window titles, which keeps brand continuity. Inter 400-600 for UI and transcripts at 15-16px with 1.5 line height. Geist Mono with tabular figures for timers, scores and cost readouts. Body text is never below 16px on mobile.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Radius 28px for windows, 20px for ornaments, 14px for cards, 999px for pills. Glass means a 40px backdrop blur at 180 percent saturate, a 1px top specular edge, and layered shadows (0 30px 80px at 45 percent black on dark). Four depth tiers: canvas, window, floating ornaments offset 16px from the window edge, and cues on top. Stacking never goes deeper than two levels.
design_language.motion: Windows spring in on open (scale 0.96 to 1, 12px rise, stiffness 260, damping 30). The orb breathes at idle and displaces with mic or persona audio level. Coach cues slide from the window edge in 200ms. Live scores tween with a digit roll. Reduced motion swaps everything for 150ms opacity fades.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 20px with a 1.5px stroke, kept from today. Glyphs sit in 36px glass circles. No emoji. Status always pairs color with a text label.
design_language.theme_modes: Dark is the default and is forced on the live-call stage. Light paper-glass is used for debrief, print and dashboard, following prefers-color-scheme with a toggle in the dock. prefers-reduced-transparency and prefers-contrast swap glass for solid fills.

navigation_and_ia: Replace the sticky header with a floating glass dock: bottom-center on desktop and a bottom dock on mobile. Items: Practice, Library, Progress, Team (manager role only), plus a Cmd+K button. Routes: /library and /library/[slug] for persona packs, /wizard for the persona builder, /brief/[scenario], /call/[id], /debrief/[id], /progress and /team. Contribute lives in the dock overflow and the footer, linking to CONTRIBUTING and persona-pack issues. During a live call the dock collapses to a single red End control, so nothing competes with the orb. Account, MFA and access-code screens move into one glass settings sheet.

screens.layout: A centered floating window, 760px wide, with a spatial four-step stepper: Source, Persona, Scenario and rubric, Test call. Step 1 is one large paste field that takes a job description, product URL, CRM notes, an ICP or a call transcript, with type chips detected as you paste. A draft card on the right fills field by field as the model streams, and each field carries a citation chip. Tapping a citation highlights the source sentence in a split view. live_coaching_and_scoring: Two channels. The persona stays on a realtime voice model (gpt-realtime over the Realtime API, with the existing ElevenLabs agent kept behind a flag) and is never asked to coach. A separate coach channel reads a rolling transcript window every 5 to 8 seconds and returns zod-validated JSON: rubric deltas, the next-best question, an objection tag and the talk-track stop. Cues follow a budget of one whisper per 20 seconds, with priority: objection alert, then next question, then talk track. Live scores render dotted until they cite a transcript turn, so no unsupported number ever shows. The debrief reconciles provisional scores with the final grade and shows the drift. Target: a cue visible within 2.5 seconds of the rep finishing a sentence.
persona_library_and_wizard: Ship about 300 persona packs at launch as plain JSON files in the repo: persona, scenario, talk track and rubric, one per job-and-industry pair across SDR, AE, customer success, collections, recruiting and the other listed jobs. Each pack is zod-validated in CI, so contributors get a fast PR check. Facets: job, industry, seniority, difficulty, objection type, channel and language. The wizard takes one paste (job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or a pasted call), fetches any URL, and asks gpt-4.1-mini (the current default) for a structured draft with a citation per field. Reps accept or edit field by field, run a test call, then save locally or export the pack as a pull request.
signature_moments: The orb's rim turns amber for a second when an objection lands, and teal when the rep hits a rubric line.
A coach cue slides out of the window edge, then docks into the talk-track rail as a completed stop.
Tapping a quote chip in the debrief scrubs the replay to that exact second, with a glass lens highlight.
The wizard's draft card fills field by field, and each citation lights its source sentence in the split view.
The debrief medallion starts dotted (provisional) and settles to solid when the final grade lands.
openai_fund_angle: Show OpenAI in the UI, not just the README. A models ribbon on the call and debrief names gpt-realtime for voice, the GPT coach model and gpt-4.1-mini for grading and the wizard, with latency, tokens and cost per call in Geist Mono. Transparent unit cost is what credit reviewers look for. Every screen has an Open prompts drawer that links to the actual prompt, rubric JSON and schema in the repo, so a contributor can edit a rubric and watch the debrief change. Contributor doors: Good first persona cards linking to labeled GitHub issues, Export as PR from the wizard, a Built with Codex badge in the hero, and Codex-assisted review of persona-pack PRs. That is a concrete Codex-for-open-source story: maintainers automate pack review, and the app runs on OpenAI models end to end.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0, behind a feature flag: install Radix Themes, add the tokens and glass recipe, keep the old classes alive. Phase 1: retheme the shell and the debrief (read-only, lowest risk). Phase 2: the live-call window, orb rebuild and coach channel. Phase 3: persona packs, library and wizard. Phase 4: progress bento and manager view. Each phase ships behind a flag and keeps voice and text parity.

risks: Glass over transcripts hurts contrast and reading speed. Mitigate with 80 percent fills on text panes and a reduced-transparency mode.
Backdrop blur plus a transmission-material orb is GPU-heavy on older laptops and phones. Cap the orb at 30 fps on mobile and fall back to a 2D gradient.
Live whispers can distract reps or arrive late. Rate-limit them, keep an off switch, and measure cue latency before enabling cues by default.
Three hundred persona packs is a content effort, and quality needs human review. Codex-assisted PR review only partly covers that.
Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli and Mindtickle already sell live-deal coaching and real-call scoring. The open-source core and the glass UX are the wedge, not a moat.
Dark-first may read as a gimmick to buyers who print debriefs. The paper-glass light mode is the answer and needs testing with real users.
